title: Real-time visualization of exo- and endocytosis membrane dynamics with confocal and super-resolution microscopy
protocol: Sterilize Locke's solution and collagenase solution using a 0.22-μm syringe filter attached to a 30-mL syringe.
Inject Locke’s solution and collagenase solution into the adrenal glands carefully with the filtered syringe.
Remove surrounding fat and connective tissue from bovine adrenal glands.
Clean the adrenal glands thoroughly with Locke's solution.
Place cleaned adrenal glands in a beaker, ready for digestion.
Open bovine adrenal glands to collect medulla.
Collect medulla and place it in Locke’s solution.
Mince collected medulla into small pieces and transfer to Locke’s solution.
Dissociate minced medulla by titrating the material with a 50-mL stripette.
Pass dissociated tissue through an 80–100 μm nylon mesh to remove bulk debris.
Pass the cells through an 80–100 μm cell strainer to remove debris.
Choose only intact glands and discard those with visible signs of internal blood coagulation.
Remove the surrounding fat and connective tissue from the glands.
Inject each gland from the adrenal vein 10–20 times with 1.5–3 mL Locke’s solution at 20°C–22°C.
Hold the syringe and maintain constant pressure for a few seconds to keep the Locke’s solution in the end of the adrenal vein.
Wash the glands with 2–3 mL collagenase solution to remove remaining Locke’s solution.
Inject the glands with 2–3 mL collagenase solution and maintain constant syringe pressure for a few seconds.
Place the glands in a glass beaker.
Cover the beaker with foil.
Incubate the beaker containing the glands in a 37°C water bath for 10 minutes.
Inject another 1-2 mL collagenase solution into the adrenal vein.
Incubate for another 10 min in the water bath after covering the beaker with foil.
Open the gland longitudinally using a sterile scissor.
Collect the cream-colored medulla section using curved fine forceps.
Transfer the collected medulla to a clean petri dish containing 50 mL Locke’s solution.
Cut the medulla tissue into small pieces using a sterilized small scissor.
Triturate the material 5-10 times with a 50-mL stripette.
Pass the dissociated material through an 80–100 μm sterilized nylon mesh to remove debris.
Collect the cells in a 50-mL conical tube.
Centrifuge at 48 × g for 3 min; discard the supernatant.
Resuspend the pellet in 20 mL Locke’s solution and triturate it with a stripette 5-10 times.
Pass the cell suspension through an 80–100 μm cell strainer.
Add fresh Locke’s solution to produce a final volume of 40–50 mL.
Centrifuge at 48 × g for another 3 min; discard the supernatant.
Resuspend the pellet in 20 mL culture medium and triturate it with a stripette 5-10 times.
Count the cell number in a Neubauer hemocytometer.
Centrifuge 2.5–3 × 10^6 cells at 48 × g for 2 min at 20°C–22°C in a 15-mL conical tube.
Discard the supernatant and resuspend the cell pellet carefully in 100 μl Nucleofector® solution per sample.
Combine 100 μl of cell suspension with 1–5 μg PH-mNG plasmid, appropriate amount of siRNA or other substrates.
Transfer cell/plasmid suspension into a certified cuvette (sample must cover the bottom of the cuvette without air bubbles).
Select program O-005 from the program list of the electroporation device.
Insert the cuvette with the cell/plasmid suspension into the Nucleofector® cuvette holder.
Start the selected program on the Nucleofector®.
Remove the cuvette from the holder once the program is complete.
Add 1,500–1,600 μL of pre-warmed culture medium to the cuvette.
Gently aspirate the cell suspension 2–3 times with a pipette.
Transfer 200–300 μL of cell suspension onto poly-D-lysine- and laminin-coated coverslips in a culture dish.
Incubate cells in a humidified 37°C/9% CO2 incubator for 1–1.5 hours.
Add 2 mL of pre-warmed culture medium to each dish.
Continue incubating the cells in a humidified 37°C/9% CO2 incubator.
Prepare patch-clamp recording pipettes with electrode resistances ranging from 2–4 MΩ after filling them with recording electrode internal solution.
Filter recording electrode internal solution using a 1-mL syringe attached with a 0.20-μm Millex-FG syringe filter unit.
Keep the internal solution on ice during the experiment.

Put the coverslip in the lower component of the magnetic chamber.

Rotate the upper component to stick all magnets of the two components.

Mount the chamber on the confocal microscope.
Place ground wire into the bath solution.

Choose a healthy transfected chromaffin cell with a smooth membrane and large cell foot.

Tap the pipette to eliminate any air bubbles in the tip.
Place the glass pipette in the pipette holder.
Apply light positive pressure through a syringe and hold by closing the valve.
Place the pipette tip in the bath using a micromanipulator.
Set the amplifier to voltage-clamp mode.
Correct the pipette offset.
Approach the coverslip with the micromanipulator, monitoring closely.
Stop moving just before touching the cell layer on the coverslip.
Change the settings of the micromanipulator to smooth and slow motion.
Approach the cell body by moving the glass pipette carefully until the tip touches the cell.
Release positive pressure and apply negative pressure gently with the syringe to obtain a giga Ω seal.
Adjust the holding potential to -80 mV and press C-fast/Auto to compensate fast capacitance.
Apply a short suction pulse using the syringe to break through the membrane.
Press C-slow/Auto to compensate slow capacitance.

Immerse coverslips in a solution containing 70 mM KCl, 60 mM NaCl, 10 mM glucose, 10 mM HEPES, 2 mM CaCl2, and 1 mM MgCl2 (pH 7.3).
Incubate the coverslips in the high potassium solution for 90 seconds.
Fix the cultures with 2% glutaraldehyde/2% paraformaldehyde/4% tannic acid/0.1 M sodium cacodylate for 15 minutes at 20°C–22°C.
Switch to a fixative solution of 2% paraformaldehyde/2% glutaraldehyde/0.1 M sodium cacodylate and incubate for another 15 minutes at 20°C–22°C.
Wash the preparation with 100 mM glycine in 0.1 M sodium cacodylate buffer for 1 minute at 20°C–22°C.
Wash the preparation three times, each time for 5 minutes, with 0.1 M sodium cacodylate at 20°C–22°C.
Treat with 1% osmium tetroxide in 0.1 M sodium cacodylate for 40 min.
Rinse in 0.1 M sodium cacodylate to wash osmium tetroxide.
Rinse in double-distilled water (DDW).
Dehydrate in ethanol: 50% Ethanol (EtOH) 1 × 5 min.
Dehydrate in ethanol: 70% EtOH 2 × 5 min.
Stain with 2% uranyl acetate in 70% EtOH for 30 min.
Dehydrate in ethanol: 70% EtOH 2 × 10 min.
Dehydrate in ethanol: 85% EtOH 2 × 5 min.
Dehydrate in ethanol: 95% EtOH 2 × 5 min.
Dehydrate in ethanol: 100% EtOH 2 × 5 min.
Place into a foil dish filled with 1:1 Epon/EtOH mix.
Replace Epon/EtOH mix with Epon resin alone for 2 h, then leave for additional 2 h.
Fill molds to brim with Epon resin.
Wipe the backs of coverslips with filter paper.
Invert coverslips over filled circular molds ensuring no air bubbles under the coverslip.
Polymerize Epon at 50°C for 14–18 h.
Transfer to a 60°C oven for several days (at least 36 h) to harden.
Immerse and hold the block in liquid nitrogen for 30 s.
Apply gentle pressure on the edge of the coverslip to remove it, ensuring no glass is left on the surface.
Trim the block.
Cut cross sections of 70 nm using a Leica UC7 Ultramicrotome.
Counterstain sections with uranyl acetate for 5 minutes.
Wash sections using distilled deionized water (DDW).
Counterstain sections with lead citrate for 3 minutes.
Wash sections using DDW.
Store the sample at 20°C–22°C in a desiccator dry box for several months if needed.
